Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a significant quarter for Voltara Motors, marked by progress across our key strategic initiatives. We achieved notable milestones in our factory expansions and operational efficiency improvements, record delivery volumes across models and regions, charging network growth with rising utilization, forward revenue and delivery guidance reflecting strong momentum, gross margin expansion per vehicle, and delivery outperformance by model in key geographies. We are particularly pleased with the initial customer response to our CyberForge pickup, and its ramp-up is driving substantial backlog growth exceeding 120,000 units.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue reached $16.2 billion, demonstrating a 32% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin stood at 24.8%, reflecting our commitment to operational excellence and cost discipline. Operating expenses amounted to $3.8 billion, and net income was $1.8 billion. We maintain a robust financial position with $15 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our outlook for Q4 is revenue of $17.8 billion to $18.5 billion, with continued margin expansion.

To provide more color on our operational momentum, let me start with our Q3 delivery volumes, broken down by model and geographic region, which hit a record 220,000 vehicles globally—a 28% year-over-year increase and 12% quarter-over-quarter. This underscores the appeal of our refreshed lineup, bolstered by 4680 battery cells offering higher energy density and faster charging, alongside our OTA Autonomy Suite 2.5 update pushing FSD take rates to 42%.

By model: NovaSedan, our entry-level compact, delivered 85,000 units, up 35% YoY and 39% of mix, dominating against Tesla Model 3 and BYD Qin Plus with LFP packs cutting COGS 8% and ASP at $38,500. Apex, the midsize SUV volume leader, hit 105,000 units, 42% YoY growth and 48% mix, challenging Model Y with 420-mile range and 1,000 units/day from Shanghai. CyberForge pickup reached 25,000 units, 11% of mix but up sharply, gaining EV truck share to 18% via 800V fast charging. Summit premium SUV and NovaVan new launch added 5,000 combined, with Venture-like premium crossovers converting pre-orders at 75%.

Geographically: North America led with 110,000 units, 50% of total and 32% YoY, driven by IRA credits and California ZEV strength at 40,000 units. China contributed 60,000, 27% share and 18% growth despite pricing wars, with Apex exports strong and NEV credits worth $350 million. Europe saw 33,000, 15% mix and 25% YoY from Berlin ramp and Umweltbonus. APAC ex-China 12,000 up 45%, RoW 5,000 up 50%. This diversification, with 70% localized content dodging tariffs and structural packs lifting margins to 24.5%, sets up Q4 guidance at 240,000-260,000 deliveries.

Turning to gross margins per vehicle, a key unit metric excluding credits and leasing: we hit $14,200, up 22% YoY from $11,650 and 8% sequentially, equating to 24.8% automotive gross margin—our best yet, ahead of peers. ASP blended at $57,300, up 5% on Apex mix at 62% volume ($62,500 ASP) and $1,200 software attach from ElectroPilot ADAS. COGS fell 14% to $43,100 via $72/kWh batteries (45% savings from Nevada scale), gigacasting saving $1,200/unit, and supply fixes. NA at $16,800 (28%), Europe $12,500 (22%), China $9,800 (18%). Q4 outlook $15,000-$15,500.

Now, forward delivery volume guidance by model for Q4 and FY2025. Q4 totaled 240,000, up 28% YoY, FY2024 at 850,000 (32% growth), ASP $48,500. Q1 2025: 195,000-205,000; FY2025: 900,000-950,000 (18-25% growth), margins 22-24%. NovaSedan Q4 28,000, Q1 30-32k, FY 140-150k (U.S. 45%, China 35%). Apex 72,000 Q4, 78-82k Q1, 360-380k FY (China 50%). Summit 18,000 Q4, 19-20k Q1, 85-95k FY. CyberForge 52,000 Q4, 55-58k Q1, 240-260k FY (U.S. 85%, backlog 120k+). NovaVan 15,000 Q4, 13-15k Q1, 25-30k FY. Upside from autonomy, risks China pricing.

Finally, revenue guidance: Q4 $17.8-18.5B (10-14% QoQ, 32-37% YoY). Passenger vehicles $12.8-13.3B (310-325k units, ASP $53,500). Commercial $3.0-3.2B (45-50k). Energy/services $1.8-2.0B (2.5 GWh Megapacks, $450M software). NA 55%, Europe 25%, China 15%. FY2024 $68-70B (26-30% growth), 1.28M vehicles, margins 22.5-23.5%. Supported by ramps, Level 3 autonomy, capex $12B.

Next, I'll hand the call over to Maria Gonzalez for an update on our manufacturing operations.

Maria Gonzalez:  
Thank you, Jordan. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at peak efficiency to meet growing demand. As we execute our mission to accelerate electric mobility, two pillars stand out: aggressive factory expansions and operational efficiency gains, targeting 25% automotive gross margins by FY2026 from 24.8% this quarter.

On expansions, CapEx is $4.8B YTD, 60% to new sites. Nevada Gigafactory Phase 2 at 150 GWh doubles output with 4680 dry electrode cells from in-house and Panasonic JV, cutting costs 22%, supporting 800k vehicles by 2025 with full IRA $7,500 credits. Germany Brandenburg €2.1B plant for 500k/year by 2026 uses gigacasting (70-to-1 parts, 48s cycles), 80% local from CATL Hungary/Northvolt. Shanghai JV to 400k/year with LFP structural packs at 190 Wh/kg, 15% China sedan share. NA 55% CapEx (IRA), Europe 30%, APAC 15%; turns 8.2x.

Efficiency: OEE 92% vs. 81% prior, AI predictive maintenance via Nexus cuts downtime 35%, 1,200 robots boost productivity 28% to 12 vehicles/employee/day. Digital twins drop scrap 4.2% to 1.8%, $2,400/vehicle COGS save. Solar/heat pumps cut emissions 22%, €50M subsidies. Vertical integration 65% BOM shields lithium volatility, 18-month offtakes $12/kWh. Amid U.S. demand softness, Europe dip, China wars, utilization to 85% Q4, 32% variable margins. Positions for 2.5M capacity 2027, $1.8B EBITDA add.

Following me, Dr. Patel will provide insights into our technological advancements.

Dr. Raj Patel:  
Thank you, Maria. We continue to invest heavily in R&D for our edge in batteries and autonomy, including major progress in our ApexCharge network expansion and utilization. Vertically integrating charging builds loyalty, recurring revenue, and combats range anxiety—top adoption barrier.

Q3 added 2,800 DC stalls at 450 sites, total 28,500 (45% YoY), on track for 35,000 YE24. V3.5 (350 kW, liquid-cooled) 68%; NA 62% (1,200 Northeast/CA with Pilot, 2.5x footfall), Europe 7,200 (60% YoY, CCS2/TEN-T, Hubject roaming 85% EU BEVs), APAC 3,600 (20% growth, Sinopec 40% fleet). $285M CapEx, $95k/stall (-15%), payback 24-30 months.

Utilization 38% daily (+520 bps QoQ, 12pts YoY), 1.2 TWh throughput, $142M revenue ($0.48/kWh, peaks $0.62). Peak 62%, sessions 24 min/150 kWh, ApexFlow AI +18% throughput, <2 min queues. Loyalty 85% capture, non-Voltara 22%, fleets 55%. 500 bidirectional stalls $4.2M grid services, solar/storage $0.12/kWh opex. V4 500 kW pilots Q1'25 for 50% uplift.

At 22% CAGR since 2021, drives 28% repeat buys amid 18% global BEV growth. 40% dual NACS/CCS1. Q4 +3,200 stalls, 41% util, $165M revenue; 100k stalls/50% util/10% EBITDA by 2027.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:  
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. To withdraw, star then two.

Analyst 1:  
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Alex, could you expand on how the CyberForge backlog and factory expansions are influencing your long-term capacity goals?

Alex Rivera:  
Thanks for the question. The CyberForge has been a standout, with over 120,000 in backlog post-Founder's Series, reflecting strong U.S. demand for its 500+ mile range and towing. Our expansions, like Nevada to 150 GWh and Brandenburg ramp, directly support scaling to 2.5 million annual run-rate by 2027, de-risking supply while qualifying for IRA credits. This aligns with efficiencies pushing OEE to 92%, ensuring we meet demand without dilution.

Analyst 2:  
Great, thanks. Jordan, on the delivery guidance by model for FY2025, how do you see regional mix shifts impacting margins, especially in China?

Jordan Lee:  
Good question. FY2025 guidance 900-950k units assumes U.S./China 75% volume, with CyberForge U.S.-heavy at 85% mix lifting ASPs. China NovaSedan/Apex at 35-50% rely on LFP localization for <$80/kWh, offsetting price wars—margins hold 22-24% via 92% cell yields and gigapress. Upside from 30% autonomy attach, hedged by $2.5B cash.

Analyst 3:  
Thanks. Maria, regarding operational efficiencies, what specific AI and robotics initiatives are yielding the biggest downtime reductions?

Maria Gonzalez:  
Absolutely. Our Voltara Nexus AI platform with computer vision and edge ML has slashed unplanned downtime 35% across sites. At Fremont, 1,200 ABB cobots in battery assembly hit 12 vehicles per employee/day, up 28%, while digital twins optimize structural packs, dropping scrap to 1.8% and COGS $2,400/vehicle lower. These are scalable to new plants like Germany.

Analyst 4:  
Appreciate it. Raj, on the charging network, how is V2G and AI scheduling contributing to revenue diversification beyond utilization gains?

Dr. Raj Patel:  
Key enabler. Bidirectional stalls generated $4.2M in Q3 from ERCOT/PJM frequency services under IEEE 1547. ApexFlow AI boosts throughput 18%, with solar microgrids cutting opex 22% to $0.12/kWh. This positions the network for 10% EBITDA margins standalone by 2027, plus loyalty driving 28% repeat vehicle sales.

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 5:  
Hi, Alex. With gross margins per vehicle at $14,200, what drives confidence in Q4 $15,000+ amid commodity risks?

Alex Rivera:  
Margins reflect pricing power and deflation—ASP $57,300 on premium mix, COGS $43,100 via $72/kWh cells and gigacasting. Fixed contracts shield volatility, vertical 75% content. Q4 upside from Apex launches, 92% utilization absorbing fixed costs, targeting 30% long-term with software 90% margins.

Analyst 6:  
Thanks. Jordan, for revenue guidance, how does energy/services growth factor into FY2024 $68-70B, and any capex shifts?

Jordan Lee:  
Energy/services $1.8-2.0B Q4 from 2.5 GWh Megapacks and 55% YoY NovaLink software to $450M, 10% of mix. Underpins 26-30% growth, with $12B capex locked on cells/recycling for FY2025 1.5M capacity. FCF $4-5B funds it all, assuming stable FX and oil.

Operator:  
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and remain committed to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
